record.paper_title: Recent Theoretical Advances and Open Problems in Nuclear Cluster Physics
record.context_brief: Carbon-12 1− α-gas state and oxygen-16 reinterpretation
record.original_question: Is the first 1− state of carbon-12 an α-gas state formed by lifting one α particle from the Hoyle state into a P shell, and, if that interpretation is confirmed, how should it change the interpretation of the fifth 0+ state of oxygen-16 that has been viewed as an α particle orbiting the carbon-12 1− state?

evidence.quote: It , therefore, can be speculated that the 1 − state corresponds to lifting an α particle from the Hoyle state into the P-shell. Also the radi us of this 1 − state is found to be enormous. It would be very important that this new ﬁndin g of this 1 − 1 state being an α gas state be conﬁrmed.
It also may then need a re-interpretation of the 5th 0 + state in 16O which is believed to consist of an α orbiting around the 1−state in 12C, see also section 3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In a microscopic α-cluster description of light self-conjugate nuclei, the second 0⁺ state of ¹²C (the Hoyle state, near 7.65 MeV) is interpreted as a dilute, weakly interacting gas of three α particles essentially condensed into an S-wave 0s orbital. Building on this picture, consider the following two linked questions:

(a) Is the first 1⁻ state of ¹²C (the lowest J^π = 1⁻ excited state, at roughly 10.84 MeV) an "α-gas" state obtained from the Hoyle state by promoting exactly one of the three α particles from the 0s orbital into a 0p (P-shell) orbital, so that the resulting state has an anomalously large root-mean-square radius characteristic of a dilute α-condensate? Provide a theoretical demonstration (e.g., via a THSR-type α-condensate wave function, RGM/GCM, or equivalent microscopic α-cluster calculation) and/or experimental confirmation (e.g., from the matter/charge radius, monopole/dipole transition strengths, and α-decay branching) that establishes or refutes this interpretation.

(b) The fifth 0⁺ state of ¹⁶O has been interpreted as a structure consisting of an α particle orbiting the 1⁻ state of ¹²C. Assuming the interpretation in (a) is confirmed, determine how this structural assignment for the fifth 0⁺ state of ¹⁶O must be revised, and exhibit a corresponding microscopic four-α (or α + ¹²C*) cluster wave function, together with predicted observables (excitation energy, radius, decay widths, and electromagnetic transition strengths) consistent with the revised interpretation.
artifact.status_search_result: Public sources confirm that the Hoyle state is well established as a dilute α-condensate, but the identification of the first 1⁻ state of ¹²C as an α-gas state with one α lifted into the P-shell is still under theoretical discussion and has not been firmly experimentally confirmed; the consequent reinterpretation of the fifth 0⁺ of ¹⁶O remains an open structural question in nuclear cluster physics.

status_evidence.title: Scientists Probe the Emergent Structure of the Carbon Nucleus
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses ongoing investigations into the cluster structure of excited states of 12C beyond the Hoyle state.
status_evidence.claim: Excited cluster states of 12C above the Hoyle state are still being actively investigated, indicating the 1- α-gas interpretation is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Structure of the Hoyle State in 12C
status_evidence.snippet: The Hoyle state is interpreted as a dilute α-condensate; higher-lying states such as the 1- and excited 0+ states are subjects of continued cluster-model studies.
status_evidence.claim: While the Hoyle state's α-condensate nature is established, the α-gas character of the 1- state and reinterpretation of 16O 0+_5 remain open.
